paper_role: architecture feasibility gate for an accelerator-resident cache data plane
question: Can multiple Neuron entry points share mutable K=2 anchor state and pass a predicted FLUX tensor between NEFFs as ranked device I/O without materializing it on the host?

frozen_system.runtime_container: one NxDModel with four routed SPMD entry points

entry_points.resident_anchor_update: one full candidate input; shift and alias K=2 anchors
entry_points.resident_predict: two FP32 coefficients only; return predicted ranked tensor
entry_points.resident_consume: ranked predicted tensor plus one FP32 scalar; stand in for scheduler/latent update
entry_points.resident_reset: one int32 request token; clear aliased anchors

frozen_system.state_identity: anchor0 and anchor1 have identical checkpoint keys, shapes, dtypes, and alias output positions in all four entry points

F1_cross_graph_state.pass_if: all full-tensor checks are bit-exact against FP32-accumulate/BF16-round host reference and reset prevents request leakage

F2_ranked_io_boundary.measured_unit: resident_predict followed by resident_consume after state is seeded

pass_if.only_host_control_inputs: two FP32 coefficients and one FP32 step scalar

F2_ranked_io_boundary.evidence: Neuron inspect nrt_tensor_write/read events grouped by NEFF execution cluster; bytes and counts are primary

scope_limit: The consume graph is an identity-scaled stand-in, not the real FLUX scheduler/latent update. Passing F1/F2 authorizes composition of the real cache-step graph, not an end-to-end speed claim.

decision.if_both_pass: Use one multi-entry NxDModel as the H1b graph boundary; next integrate scheduler and resident latent, then connect full-DiT anchor output through ranked I/O.
decision.if_state_fails: The current legacy ModelBuilder cannot implement a shared-state multi-NEFF cache service; redraw as one stateful entry point or adopt ModelBuilder v2.
decision.if_boundary_fails: Do not claim accelerator-resident inter-NEFF dataflow; fuse producer/consumer or keep the claim at host-controlled multi-graph execution.
